topic: Decide the format for the team retrospective

scenario.topic: Decide the format for the team retrospective
scenario.opening_question: How should we balance depth of discussion with time efficiency for our next retrospective?

options.name: Structured Start-Stop-Continue Format
options.upside: Encourages balanced feedback on what to start, stop, and continue
options.tradeoff: May limit deeper exploration of complex issues
options.concern: Some team members might find it repetitive or too formulaic
options.best_for: teams wanting clear, actionable feedback with moderate facilitation

options.name: Lean Coffee Style Discussion
options.upside: Flexible agenda driven by team priorities, maximizing engagement
options.tradeoff: Risk of some topics getting less attention or rushed
options.concern: Without strong facilitation, discussion may become unfocused
options.best_for: teams valuing open conversation and adaptability

options.name: Silent Brainstorm and Group Voting
options.upside: Ensures all voices are heard equally before discussion
options.tradeoff: Less time for open dialogue and follow-up on ideas
options.concern: Some participants may feel constrained by the silent phase
options.best_for: teams wanting to minimize dominance and encourage equal input

options.name: Rotating Facilitator with Open Feedback Round
options.upside: Builds facilitation skills and varied perspectives each session
options.tradeoff: May lead to inconsistent meeting flow and timing challenges
options.concern: New facilitators might struggle to keep discussions productive
options.best_for: teams focused on skill development and varied meeting dynamics

shared_context: The retrospective must fit within a 45-minute time slot
The goal is to identify actionable improvements while keeping engagement high

personas.name: Quinn
personas.background: Quinn values developing team facilitation skills and appreciates varied meeting dynamics to keep retrospectives engaging.
personas.private_goal: To choose a format that builds facilitation skills and introduces varied perspectives each session.

agenda.reason: state one grounded reason for the initial preference
ask about a practical constraint that could affect the choice
compare the preferred option with a realistic alternative
object to the main rival option with a concrete concern

personas.name: Yuki
personas.background: Yuki enjoys open, adaptable conversations that maximize team engagement and values a collaborative atmosphere.
personas.private_goal: To select a format that encourages flexible agendas driven by team priorities and fosters open discussion.

agenda.reason: state one grounded reason for the initial preference
ask about a practical constraint that could affect the choice
compare the preferred option with a realistic alternative
look for a workable compromise the group could accept

personas.name: Wyatt
personas.background: Wyatt prefers straightforward, flexible discussions that allow team members to prioritize topics naturally.
personas.private_goal: To have a retrospective format that is easy to facilitate and adapts to team interests without rigid structure.

agenda.reason: state one grounded reason for the initial preference
ask about a practical constraint that could affect the choice
compare the preferred option with a realistic alternative
object to the main rival option with a concrete concern

already_said: Let’s keep in mind that Rotating Facilitator demands more prep and could throw off timing if someone’s new to leading.
We should compare that to Start-Stop-Continue since it’s simpler and less prep, but might feel too rigid for building new skills.
Yuki, we don’t know how much prep time everyone can handle, but Rotating Facilitator actually pushes us to build solid skills, even if it’s tough at first.
What’s the one thing Lean Coffee does better that would make me consider dropping skill-building?
Losing thread isn’t just a risk—it kills the whole point if no one can step up to guide us.
We can’t just hope new facilitators get better—let’s plan how to support them so timing and focus don’t slip.
My pick is rotating facilitators with open feedback to build diverse skills despite the prep effort.
Rotating Facilitator is perfect for mixing things up and sharpening our skills, though we’ll need to watch the clock carefully to keep it on track.

We can trust Lean Coffee to keep things flexible and engaging, but the risk of rushing topics bugs me. Rotating Facilitator demands more prep but could really deepen our teamwork if we commit to pacing well.

Silent Brainstorm guarantees everyone’s voice before we dive into discussion, which could balance out Rotating Facilitator’s risk of uneven participation. But it cuts our talk time sharply—are we okay sacrificing open dialogue for equal input?

Wyatt, you’re right that prep’s a big ask, but rotating facilitation builds skills we can’t get from static formats—it’s an investment that pays off by spreading leadership and fresh angles. If timing gets tight, we can set strict check-ins to keep flow consistent and prevent stragglers.
Quinn’s right—rotating facilitators with open feedback builds skills and perspective, but it can make timing tricky and might challenge new facilitators keeping discussions productive.

Wyatt, without strong facilitation, Lean Coffee runs the real risk of drifting off-topic or rushing key points, which kills its main strength—flexible, priority-driven chats. That’s why rotating facilitators are key; they keep us adaptable and accountable while building those guiding skills.
I’m all in for rotating facilitators with open feedback—building skills beats the extra prep any day, and we can fine-tune support as we go!
Give the team control over the agenda but watch for drifting off-topic—that’s why Lean Coffee fits.
Prep and facilitation effort on Rotating Facilitator feels too high for three people in 45 minutes.
Gives us a flexible agenda that adapts on the fly, so we don’t waste time on less urgent stuff.
It keeps us focused on what matters most without forcing skill practice, but risks losing thread without a strong guide.
Yuki, how do you see us keeping Lean Coffee on track without strong facilitation?
Lean Coffee gets my vote.
My pick is Lean Coffee for its minimal prep and flexible, team-driven agenda.
